intro: Lesson 9. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ (١) وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ (٢) وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ (٣) وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ (٤) وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ (٥)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And has responded to its Lord and was obligated [to do so]
And when the earth has been extended
And has cast out that within it and relinquished [it]
And has responded to its Lord and was obligated [to do so] -

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 84:1-5 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Which ayah repeats 84:2 word for word?
Listening rota: today's group recites 84:1-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, write what the earth does in 84:3 to 4.
questions.a: It is spread out, throws out what is in it and becomes empty.

questions.q: 84:2 and 84:5 are the same words. How can a repeated ayah help or trick your memory?
questions.a: It helps (one ayah learned twice) but can trick you into skipping 84:3 to 4; link 84:4 to 84:5 carefully.
A) listened to and obeyed. 84:2: 'and has listened to its Lord and was obligated', meaning it obeyed.

questions.q: Al-Inshiqaq 84:3: «وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: What would it look like if the sky split open? Why does the Qur'an describe the Day of Judgement so vividly?
questions.a: So that we remember it and prepare: the sky and the earth obey their Lord on that Day (84:1 to 5).
